code_label: QML advantage not yet clearly demonstrated
text_span: Quantum Machine Learning (QML) hasn’t yet demonstrated extensively and clearly its advantages compared to the classical machine learning approach.
rationale: States the paper’s motivating problem and research gap.

code_label: LDA improves quantum classifier preprocessing
text_span: This study shows that we can achieve better classical encoding and performance of quantum classiﬁers by using Linear Discriminant Analysis (LDA) during the data preprocessing step.
rationale: Summarizes the main claimed finding about preprocessing.

code_label: VQA gains balanced accuracy with LDA
text_span: Variational Quantum Algorithm (VQA) shows a gain of performance in balanced accuracy with the LDA technique and outperforms baseline classical classiﬁers.
rationale: Highlights the headline performance claim.

code_label: NISQ noise and limited qubits constrain QML
text_span: The current quantum computers are noisy and have few qubits to test, making it difﬁcult to demonstrate the current and potential quantum advantage of QML methods.
rationale: Identifies a central practical constraint shaping the study.

code_label: Business context requires methods for big datasets on NISQ devices
text_span: To be practical in a business context, QML techniques need to avoid the small number of qubits constraint and create a methodology to use big datasets on the current NISQ devices.
rationale: States the applied motivation for the work.

code_label: Study compares preprocessing and classifier methods
text_span: In this paper, we approach the input problem by comparing different preprocessing methods and classiﬁer methods on small and larger datasets with a binary target.
rationale: Defines the comparative study design.

code_label: LDA better than PCA for many features
text_span: We demonstrate that using Linear Discriminant Analysis (LDA) within the preprocessing phase is better than Principal Component Analysis (PCA) when the dataset possesses an important number of features.
rationale: States a key comparative claim about dimensionality reduction.

code_label: Two datasets selected to emulate real business cases
text_span: The dataset selection in this research aims to emulate real business cases scenario where the users can ﬁnd imbalanced dataframes, a small or large number of features
rationale: Explains dataset selection criteria.

code_label: Credit card dataset is imbalanced
text_span: This data is imbalanced, having 22% of defaulters and 78% of non-defaulters.
locator: 2.1 UCI - Default of Credit Card Clients Dataset
rationale: Describes a key dataset property relevant to classification difficulty.

code_label: Fraud dataset has 114 features and imbalance
text_span: This data was extracted from Kaggle and was originally uploaded by Volodymyr Gavrish3.
rationale: Identifies the source and context of the second dataset; the surrounding paragraph also states 114 features and class imbalance.

code_label: PCA is common for QML dimensionality reduction
text_span: PCA is one of the predominant structures for dimensionality reduction in the exploration of classic data into QML algorithms
rationale: Positions PCA as a standard baseline preprocessing method.

code_label: LDA uses class labels to maximize separability
text_span: LDA is a supervised method that considers class labels by reducing the number of dimensions.
rationale: Defines the supervised nature of LDA.

code_label: Benchmark includes classical and quantum classifiers
text_span: we benchmark classical classiﬁers such as Logistic Regression, Decision Tree, Random Forest, K-Nearest Neighbors, SVM, Quantum Kernel (QSVC), and Variational Quantum Algorithm
rationale: Lists the model families compared in the study.

code_label: Evaluation uses 10-fold cross-validation
text_span: The models are benchmarked with k-fold cross-validation with 10 folds.
rationale: Specifies the evaluation protocol.

code_label: Simulators used for fast iteration
text_span: The objective behind using simulators alone in this research is that we can have fast iterations, adjustments, and results.
rationale: Explains why simulator backends were chosen.

code_label: Noise subtracted from simulations
text_span: In our case, we subtracted the noise from the simulations.
rationale: States a specific simulation choice affecting results.

code_label: Only two qubits chosen for business-context demonstration
text_span: Only two qubits were chosen through this study to show the usability of a small number of qubits in a business context.
rationale: Describes a central design constraint of the experiments.

code_label: Quantum encoding uses feature maps and angle encoding
text_span: In this study, we used a quantum feature map (Qiskit ZZFeatureMap) and angle encoding (Pennylane) to be used with QSVC and VQC respectively.
rationale: Specifies the quantum data encoding methods.

code_label: UCI baseline classical models struggle on imbalance
text_span: The baseline demonstrates that classical methods struggle to create a good classiﬁer to separate the minority class from the majority class.
rationale: Summarizes baseline performance on the first dataset.

code_label: UCI best classical precision and f1 are low
text_span: The precision is at a maximum of 38.74% for the KNN, and the best f1-score is reached by CART with a small value of 39.10%.
rationale: Reports the strongest classical baseline numbers on the UCI dataset.

code_label: UCI QSVC with SKPP fails to separate classes
text_span: QSVC with the SKPP technique shows metrics with 0.00%, meaning a non-separation between both classes.
rationale: Identifies a failed quantum configuration.

code_label: UCI LDA best for both quantum algorithms
text_span: LDA is the best dimensionality reduction for both quantum algorithms.
rationale: States the best-performing preprocessing choice for the UCI quantum models.

code_label: UCI VQA with LDA reaches very high balanced accuracy
rationale: Captures the strongest reported UCI quantum result in the table.

code_label: Fraud baseline classical models perform well
text_span: Table 4 shows the results for the baseline for the fraud (bank) detection dataset with classical ML.
rationale: Introduces the baseline results for the second dataset.

code_label: Fraud quantum algorithms provide small advantage over LDA
text_span: Even if the baseline classical ML models perform well, the quantum algorithms provide a small advantage over the LDA approach
rationale: States the comparative conclusion for the fraud dataset.

code_label: PCA worst representation for QSVC on fraud dataset
text_span: PCA demonstrates the worst representation for QSVC
rationale: Identifies the weakest preprocessing choice for one quantum model.

code_label: LDA best for both QSVC and VQA on fraud dataset
text_span: LDA shows the best results for both QSVC and VQA.
rationale: States the best-performing preprocessing choice on the second dataset.

code_label: Four quantum algorithms beat best baseline precision
text_span: four quantum algorithms beat the best precision value of the baseline
rationale: Highlights a specific comparative advantage claim.

code_label: LDA may provide better data representation for qubits
text_span: LDA shows more promising results for supervised machine learning tasks with quantum computers.
rationale: Generalizes the observed LDA effect across the study.

code_label: Quantum advantage framed as better information extraction
text_span: quantum advantage doesn’t need to be measured by the ability to beat classical ML models but can be regarded as a better information extraction technique.
rationale: Provides the authors’ interpretive framing of quantum advantage.

code_label: Need to study LDA versus PCA further
text_span: The prevalence of LDA under PCA wasn’t explored in this paper but will be explored in future to understand how LDA provides a better data representation for qubits encoding.
rationale: Explicitly states a future research direction.

code_label: Need to study PCA in unsupervised tasks
text_span: Also, we will study the potential impact of PCA in unsupervised tasks.
rationale: Another stated future work item.

code_label: Classical methods not tuned specifically
text_span: Classical ML methods selected for this study weren’t tuned speciﬁcally on the two datasets.
rationale: States a methodological caveat affecting interpretation.

code_label: Default parameters used for classical models
text_span: Default parameters were chosen.
rationale: Indicates a limitation in model optimization.

code_label: LR did not converge on fraud dataset
text_span: on the fraud detection dataset, the default limit was reached and LR wasn’t converging.
rationale: Reports a concrete convergence problem.

code_label: Feature map and ansatz not tuned
text_span: The parameters of the feature map weren’t tuned but ﬁxed through the study with a number of repetitions of 2 and a feature dimension of 2.
rationale: States a fixed-parameter limitation for the quantum models.

code_label: Need to explore different ansatzes
text_span: An interesting perspective will also to study the impact of different ansatzes on the VQA results.
rationale: Explicit future work on variational circuit design.

code_label: Need more datasets and domains for general benchmark
text_span: we need to extend the approach with other datasets (higher number of features) in other domains to create a benchmark through a general application.
rationale: States the need for broader validation.
